knowledge:
- key_parameters: data=A log2-transformed intensity matrix (with missing values as NA), a SummarizedExperiment, or an MSnSet object ;; design=A formula or design matrix specifying the experimental conditions ;; col_data=A data frame containing sample annotations corresponding to the columns of the data matrix ;; reference_level=The name of the condition to be used as the reference/intercept (e.g., negative control) ;; contrast=A string or expression specifying the comparison of interest (e.g., "conditionCG1407" or Condition_1 - Condition_2) ;; reduced_model=Used instead of contrast to perform a likelihood ratio F-test
- alternatives: imputation-based methods=Existing methods replace missing values with reasonable numbers (imputation) before running classical methods, but this obscures the amount of available information and can lead to over-confident predictions ;; quantile normalization=Distorts data to make all distributions equal, which is problematic because missing values shift the observed intensity distribution; median_normalization() is preferred ;; base R dist()=Cannot handle missing values, whereas dist_approx() estimates expected distance without imputation
- when_to_use: When analyzing label-free mass spectrometry (LFQ) proteomics data with a high proportion of missing values (especially at low intensities/dropout)
- pitfalls: Coding missing values as 0 instead of NA (MaxQuant outputs missing values as 0, which must be explicitly converted to NA and log2-transformed before running proDA) ;; Using quantile normalization on datasets with varying missing value rates, which distorts the true intensity distributions ;; Using standard distance calculations (like base R dist()) which fail with NA values or require problematic imputation

workflows.name: differential_abundance_analysis
workflows.intent: Identify differentially abundant proteins in label-free mass spectrometry data by fitting a probabilistic dropout model without imputation.
input: proteinGroups.txt (MaxQuant output table containing protein IDs and LFQ intensity columns)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the protein intensity data and convert zero values to NA ;; 2. Log2-transform the intensities ;; 3. Perform median normalization using median_normalization() ;; 4. Estimate sample distances using dist_approx() ;; 5. Fit the probabilistic dropout model using proDA() ;; 6. Test for differential abundance using test_diff()
workflows.code:
maxquant_protein_table <- read.delim(
    system.file("extdata/proteinGroups.txt", package = "proDA", mustWork = TRUE),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
intensity_colnames <- grep("^LFQ\\.intensity\\.", colnames(maxquant_protein_table), value=TRUE)
abundance_matrix <- as.matrix(maxquant_protein_table[, intensity_colnames])
colnames(abundance_matrix) <- sub("^LFQ\\.intensity\\.", "", intensity_colnames)
rownames(abundance_matrix) <- maxquant_protein_table$Protein.IDs
abundance_matrix[abundance_matrix == 0] <- NA
abundance_matrix <- log2(abundance_matrix)
normalized_abundance_matrix <- median_normalization(abundance_matrix)
da <- dist_approx(normalized_abundance_matrix)
sample_info_df <- data.frame(name = colnames(normalized_abundance_matrix),
                             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
sample_info_df$condition <- substr(sample_info_df$name, 1, nchar(sample_info_df$name)  - 3)
sample_info_df$replicate <- as.numeric(
  substr(sample_info_df$name, nchar(sample_info_df$name)  - 1, 20)
)
fit <- proDA(normalized_abundance_matrix, design = ~ condition, 
             col_data = sample_info_df, reference_level = "S2R")
test_res <- test_diff(fit, "conditionCG1407")
